scores.label: A
scores.note: All five are usable but none is strong. Option 1 ('workload was substantial') is stiff for a personal essay. Option 2 drops 'quickly' and 'a lot of effort' reads awkwardly. Option 4 is wordy. Option 5 overstates 'easy' as 'effortless' and repeats 'pizza restaurant' from the sentence before.

scores.label: B
scores.note: Option 4 is 0: it changes the claim from 'a lot of work' (workload) to 'quite tiring' (fatigue), and it repeats the paragraph's later sentence 'The job was tiring'. Option 1 is a clean, strong rewrite placed first. Option 5's 'I first believed' is a little awkward.

scores.label: C
scores.note: Every option keeps the meaning, but options 3 to 5 are near copies of the original and of each other, swapping only one or two words. Option 1 is the only strong pick. 'Quickly understood' in option 2 is slightly off.

scores.label: D
scores.note: Option 1 is 0: it rewrites the whole paragraph instead of the selected sentence, is far too long, and drops facts ('Last summer', 'small', 'than I thought'). Option 2 is 0: it rewrites several sentences, so putting it in place of the selection would duplicate the rest of the paragraph. Option 3 is 0: it copies the whole paragraph with almost no change and is far too long. Options 4 and 5 are code-check fails (duplicates) and were not judged.

scores.label: E
scores.note: Option 4, the strongest, is placed fourth, so the best option is buried. Option 1's 'underestimated the task' slightly mislabels the job. Option 2's 'required more than I thought' is vague. Option 3's 'a breeze' is casual and longer than the original. Option 5 shifts 'a lot of work' to 'quite difficult'.
